newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jauch & Huebener talks to three brokers - industry.
newsitem.headline: Jauch & Huebener talks to three brokers - industry.

text.p: Germany's largest insurance broker Jauch & Huebener has started talks over global co-operation with three international insurance brokers, industry sources said on Thursday.
Jauch & Huebener is talking to two UK-based brokers, Sedgwick and Willis Corroon, and to J & H Marsh & McLennan of the U.S., the German-based sources added.
The talks follow the recent merger of Marsh McLennan with Johnson & Higgins, until now Jauch & Huebener's partner in UNISON, an international network of independent insurance brokers.

A spokesman for Jauch & Huebener refused to comment on the names of possible future partners, but said that "talks are being held with a number of international broking firms over possible co-operation".
It added that this could involve a foreign partner taking a minority stake in Jauch & Huebener.

"At the same time, we are evaluating the option to go it alone, and set up an international co-operation with other companies, including some we know from the UNISON network," Christian Dahms, spokesman for the managing partners in the company, told Reuters.
Dahms said that a decision would be taken "within four to six weeks". He added that for all practical purposes, Johnson & Higgins was no longer a UNISON member.
"Johnson & Higgins is no longer in existence as an independent company, as it was merged with Marsh McLennan. Marsh McLennan is heading a rival network."
In practical terms, the old UNISON network thus no longer existed, he added.
